chapter: Stuff Smith Trio and New York
title: Meeting John Levy in 1937 in Tony Fambro's band
summary: Playing piano in Tony Fambro's Chicago band that battled Nat Cole's orchestra, then the trip to Indianapolis and stranding.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: When did you first meet John?

Oh, let's see. 1937, I can tell you. We were working with a local band and I was called in to play piano in this particular band because -- the name of the band was the Tony [Fanborough](PHONETIC), and they used to have battles of jazz with the Nat Cole Orchestra. And Nat had a big band, you know. It was just like he almost looked like Earl Hines on piano. He dressed like him.
Was it a conscious effort to resemble Earl Hines, do you think, or was it just the fact that there was some natural resemblance?
Well, there was a natural, but everybody around Chicago at that time -- excuse me -- admired Earl Hines. He had a great influence on all piano players, you know?
And that's when I first joined this band with John, and then we formed a little group and went to

And came back in John's big 1931 Buick. Now this was -- we're just about 1940 now, and we got back home. We did some little working around, different clubs around Chicago, you know. And when John got me with Stuff and that's probably one of the best moves that has happened to me.
